report:
Reviewed the complete current crates.sage_ir.types.body.conditional_patterns claim and all associated evidence from the fresh start. It requires each of if-let, while-let, and let chains to lower into structured match and control-flow forms. None of those three source families can be omitted when establishing the guarantee; merely carrying a source-shaped conditional-pattern node is insufficient. Captured the relevant typed-IR design table, accepted completed-tree rationale, and current if-let/while-let checker branches as dependencies.

There is exactly one implementation association: the sage_meta::todo marker in crates/sage-meta/tests/representation_spec.rs stating that complete conditional-pattern elaboration and tree fixtures remain pending. The only associated test is sage_meta::todo::types_body_conditional_patterns, whose entire body is that explanatory TODO, without assertions. It therefore supplies an explicit test deferral, not behavioral coverage. There are no ordinary or N/A evidence entries for this anchor.

Inspection of the current checker confirms the elaboration prerequisite. The if-let branch checks scrutinee and pattern, introduces a scope for the then branch, relates branch result types, and returns TyExprData::IfLet. The while-let branch checks the scrutinee/pattern/body under a scope and returns TyExprData::WhileLet with unit type. These partial checks do not themselves perform the specified structured match/control-flow elaboration. The captured neighboring Match and Loop constructors are available representation paths but their existence does not establish a transformation from either source form. No current assertion demonstrates let-chain elaboration, and this review does not infer it from single-pattern handling. The associated complete-elaboration TODO covers that third required family as well.

The deferral is justified by the pending transformation and direct tree fixtures. Replacing it requires associated tests visibly checking the resulting structured forms for if-let (including alternatives), while-let (including repeated matching and termination), and let chains (including dependent bindings and conditional progression), so scope handling and source-shape retention cannot masquerade as completed lowering. These are future validation requirements, not claims of executed tests or implemented behavior. The accepted architecture keeps structured trees above MIR and does not require basic-block lowering for this claim.

Validation performed was source inspection with review start/read. No source modifications or behavioral tests were performed; centralized suites remain separate evidence. All requirements are accounted for as explicitly deferred, with no weakened specification and no ordinary completeness verdict. No requested edits are needed to preserve the existing honest implementation/test TODO.
